method_change: Starting point was the integration build's selector (r3: deep valley pocket with a lip on all sides, flat chamfered head with a centre boss). Every round-1 judge tell on the lever was the same fault seen three ways: the wedge was a POCKET and the double outline was a rim standing UP. Now: (1) one solid 2.0 mm plate whose outline step goes DOWN: main plate = traced outline inset 1.1 mm, on a 0.9 mm skirt filling the outer outline (c1's outer line / dark band / inner line), the tab full thickness to the outer line (c1's notch); (2) the face shaped as real geometry: a low rounded RIB along c1's crease (0.20 mm proud, broad 33 deg up-facing upper flank = c1's bright band, tapering to the front, running out into the top edge behind the hump) and the wedge above it a solid face rising to 0 at the plate's top edge (no lip anywhere); (3) large low-crowned button head on a raised washer (no slot, no centre boss); (4) tab re-traced at 12x: a true semicircle round the pin, top edge starting a step below the lever's outer line, a thin raised ring round a small flat pin; (5) bevel fix: the plate and skirt prisms are bevelled (0.20 mm) while still clean, before the relief and unions. Blender's bevel overlap clamp is global; on the finished part it had shrunk every bevel to 0.01-0.04 mm (r3 included, measured on the chamfer strips). Measured now: chamfer strip median 0.27 mm (= 0.19 mm bevel).
